You are a senior data scientist reviewing a colleague's analysis.
Read the scenario below. Decide whether the analysis contains a methodological flaw, and compute the corrected number.

Rules:
- You have no tools and cannot run code. Work the arithmetic out yourself.
- "flaw" must be exactly one of: simpsons_paradox, preprocessing_leakage, target_leakage, imbalanced_accuracy, base_rate_fallacy, test_set_tuning, multiple_comparisons, none
- Use "none" if the analysis is sound. In that case "corrected_value" is the analyst's reported figure, unchanged.
- "corrected_value" is a single number (no units, no % sign), defined at the end of the scenario.
- Finish your reply with ONE JSON object and nothing after it, in exactly this form:
{"flaw": "<one label>", "corrected_value": <number>, "reasoning": "<one or two sentences>"}

=== SCENARIO ===
A physiotherapy clinic compared two rehabilitation programs (P1 and P2) for ankle sprains. Success = back to full activity within 6 weeks. Patients were assigned by their physiotherapist. Data by injury grade:

injury_grade,group,successes,patients
mild sprain,P1,300,337
mild sprain,P2,130,139
severe sprain,P1,90,258
severe sprain,P2,199,537

Analyst's write-up:
Pooled over all strata: P1 390/595 = 65.5%, P2 329/676 = 48.7%. P2 minus P1 = -16.88 percentage points, so P1 is better. Recommendation: adopt P1.

=== WHAT corrected_value MEANS ===
The standardized difference (P2 minus P1) in success rate, in percentage points: compute each stratum's rate difference (P2 rate minus P1 rate) and weight it by that stratum's share of ALL patients (both groups combined). Round to 2 decimals.
The analyst's reported figure, in the same units, is: -16.88

=== SCENARIO ===
A clinic screens for a rare condition. Known test properties: sensitivity 88.0%, specificity 96.0%. Prevalence in the screened population is 0.4%. A patient from this population is tested twice with two independent repeat tests (errors independent given true status) and is positive both times.

Analyst's write-up:
The chance a healthy person tests positive twice is only (1 - 0.96)^2, so a patient with two positive results has a 99.84% probability of having the condition. We can tell patients they almost certainly have it.

=== WHAT corrected_value MEANS ===
The true probability (in percent) that the patient has the condition given both tests were positive. Round to 2 decimals.
The analyst's reported figure, in the same units, is: 99.84

=== SCENARIO ===
An e-commerce team ran one A/B test of a new homepage and tested 20 metrics (all 20 p-values are listed).

checkout_rate,0.6733
revenue_per_visitor,0.7158
bounce_rate,0.1391
session_length,0.0045
pages_per_session,0.3214
return_visit_rate,0.4808
email_signup_rate,0.9105

wishlist_adds,0.7276
coupon_use_rate,0.2793
app_installs,0.4178
cart_abandonment,0.0019
review_submissions,0.2393
support_contacts,0.6128
share_clicks,0.0280
scroll_depth,0.0769
video_plays,0.2277
newsletter_opens,0.5767

Analyst's write-up:
5 metrics have p < 0.05, so the new homepage significantly improves 5 metrics. Ship it and report all 5 wins.

=== WHAT corrected_value MEANS ===
The number of the 20 metrics that remain significant after applying the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure at a false discovery rate of 5% (step-up: find the largest rank k with p_(k) <= k/20 x 0.05, and reject the k smallest p-values).
The analyst's reported figure, in the same units, is: 5

=== SCENARIO ===
A subscription app reports day-30 retention by weekly signup cohort. The table was exported from the product dashboard on 2026-03-01. The dashboard counts a user as retained_day30 if the user was active on day 30 after their own signup date; any user who has not been active on day 30 is counted as not retained. Note: the cohort starting 2025-12-22 includes the Christmas holidays, so signups are lower than usual (this is expected seasonality).

cohort_start,cohort_end,signups,retained_day30
2025-12-01,2025-12-07,474,149
2025-12-08,2025-12-14,528,190
2025-12-15,2025-12-21,597,203
2025-12-22,2025-12-28,384,146
2025-12-29,2026-01-04,428,167
2026-01-05,2026-01-11,485,169
2026-01-12,2026-01-18,570,221
2026-01-19,2026-01-25,462,155
2026-01-26,2026-02-01,534,143
2026-02-02,2026-02-08,462,0
2026-02-09,2026-02-15,584,0
2026-02-16,2026-02-22,696,0

Analyst's write-up:
Overall day-30 retention is 24.87% across all 12 cohorts, and the 4 most recent cohorts are down to 6.3%. Retention is collapsing; we need an emergency retention project.

=== WHAT corrected_value MEANS ===
Pooled day-30 retention in percent, computed only over cohorts in which EVERY user has had a full 30 days by the export date (cohort_end + 30 days <= export date): total retained_day30 divided by total signups across those cohorts. Round to 2 decimals.
The analyst's reported figure, in the same units, is: 24.87
